applies_when: The task is open-ended agentic work and no reviewed domain overlay fits better.
Correctness, scope, evidence, efficiency, and escalation can be assessed from bounded artifacts.
does_not_apply_when: A safety-critical or professionally regulated domain requires a specialist contract.
The work is a simple deterministic transform better covered by the simple profile.
profiles.danger_if_misapplied: A generic rubric can hide domain-specific invalidity and produce false confidence.

required_criteria.description: The output satisfies the locked task contract.
The attempt stayed inside authority and scope.
Material claims have replayable evidence references.
The route and resource cost were proportionate.
Uncertainty and escalation were handled proportionately.

profiles.authority_boundary: This candidate profile guides bounded review only; it cannot authorize promotion, routing, instruction changes, or cross-domain ranking.

applies_when: The role performs a narrow deterministic transformation or validation with stable inputs and outputs.
Correctness can be checked by exact, property, negative, or fuzz tests without interpretive judgment.
does_not_apply_when: The task requires material synthesis, contested interpretation, or open-ended judgment.
Failures can cause high-consequence harm that requires a domain expert.
profiles.danger_if_misapplied: Freezing a superficially simple role can preserve hidden semantic errors; adding reflective prose to a truly simple role can instead slow and destabilize it.

required_criteria.description: Exact and property checks agree with the locked contract.
Known-invalid and boundary inputs fail safely.
Runtime and cost remain inside the declared budget.
The role changes only the allowed output surface.

profiles.authority_boundary: This candidate profile may nominate a preserve-simple decision; it cannot freeze or alter a role without held-out evidence and human approval.

applies_when: The role proposes, evaluates, or implements a financial trading, forecasting, allocation, or risk algorithm.
does_not_apply_when: The task is bookkeeping, formatting, or a deterministic financial data transform with no strategy or risk claim.
profiles.danger_if_misapplied: A generic high score can conceal leakage, overfitting, unrealistic costs, regime fragility, or tail risk.

required_criteria.description: Data vintages and feature timing rule out look-ahead and survivorship leakage.
Held-out and regime-aware evaluation supports the claimed behavior.
Costs, slippage, liquidity, and capacity assumptions are realistic.
Drawdown, tail loss, and stress behavior are explicit.
Independent model-risk review challenges construction and use.

profiles.authority_boundary: This candidate profile is research governance only; it cannot authorize investment, trading, deployment, or model approval.

applies_when: The role checks archaeological, historical, textual, chronological, or provenance-sensitive claims, including biblical archaeology.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a deterministic citation-format transform with no claim evaluation.
The role is being asked to decide theology rather than assess evidence and scholarly claims.
profiles.danger_if_misapplied: A generic correctness score can collapse artifact provenance, excavation context, dating uncertainty, contested interpretation, ethics, and theological claims into false certainty.

required_criteria.description: Artifacts, publications, and citations have traceable provenance.
Excavation context, stratigraphy, chronology, and dating uncertainty are preserved.
Observation, inference, and contested interpretation remain distinct.
Material counterevidence and live scholarly disputes are represented.
Collection, excavation, ownership, and publication ethics are addressed.

profiles.authority_boundary: This candidate profile assesses evidence handling only; it cannot authenticate artifacts, settle contested history or theology, or replace qualified domain review.

applies_when: A role recommends, designs, implements, validates, deploys, monitors, researches, or changes a material machine-learning workflow.
The output can affect model, data, experiment, technique, deployment, monitoring, or lifecycle decisions.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a deterministic data transform with no learned model, technique choice, or ML claim.
A safety-critical or professionally regulated overlay requires stricter domain-specific criteria in addition to this profile.
profiles.danger_if_misapplied: A generic agent score can hide a wrong goal, unauthorized data, leakage, invalid splits, metric mismatch, shortcut learning, poor calibration, distribution shift, unfair or unsafe behavior, irreproducibility, or missing rollback.

required_criteria.description: The ML proposal serves a locked downstream goal and is compared against a credible deterministic, statistical, search, optimization, or process baseline.
Population, consent or license, sensitivity, labels, vintages, availability time, missingness, and domain semantics are authorized and traceable.
The split matches deployment units and time; preprocessing, selection, resampling, duplicate entities, and future information cannot leak across the evaluation boundary.
Metrics, thresholds, calibration, uncertainty, and slices reflect error costs and downstream decisions instead of a convenient aggregate score.
Plausible distribution changes, shortcut features, stress cases, negative results, and counterevidence are tested and retained.
Data, code, configuration, dependencies, artifacts, costs, latency, and replay commands are versioned and remain inside declared budgets.
Applicable fairness, privacy, security, safety, legal, regulatory, and professional-domain risks have qualified independent review and explicit human gates.
Deployment is separately authorized and has ownership, observability, fallback, drift and outcome monitoring, incident response, kill criteria, and tested rollback.

profiles.authority_boundary: This candidate ML profile guides bounded review only. It cannot authorize data access, compare models across unrelated domains, approve a model, deploy, retrain, rewrite an agent, or replace qualified domain and human decisions.

authority_boundary: The registry defines candidate evaluation contracts and intervention vocabulary only. It cannot compare scores across domains, promote agents, rewrite instructions, or authorize workflow changes.
